name: result-driven-spatial-link
title: Result-Driven Spatial Linkage — Coloring AS Nodes by Model Readout (Planned)
question:
Can the placeholder `readout` string on every (model, AS-node) spatial
link be replaced with a real steady-state species concentration drawn
from the committed corpus COPASI/Tellurium comparison dataset, so the 3D
viewer colors nodes by an actual result instead of by coverage/presence
alone?

study_card.goal: Extract steady-state species concentrations from the committed corpus COPASI/Tellurium comparison dataset and attach them as the `readout` field on each (model, AS-node) link, replacing the placeholder 'pending time-series' string; re-render the 3D viewer pack colored by that value.
study_card.mechanism: Planned: a readout-extraction Step reusing spatial-linkage's join output (10 links/5 models today) plus the committed corpus simulation dataset, resolving each linked model's final/steady-state timepoint per shared species and attaching it as `readout`; downstream viewer-pack generation recolors nodes by that value instead of a boolean covered/uncovered flag.
study_card.expected_result: Every (model, AS-node) link that has a corresponding entry in the committed corpus dataset carries a real numeric readout; links with no matching dataset entry remain explicitly flagged as unresolved rather than silently defaulting.
study_card.main_expert_question: Which species/readout should be chosen when a model has many state variables (e.g. glucose vs insulin vs glycogen) — a single canonical readout per organ, or a viewer-selectable set?
study_card.future_work: The real readout-extraction and re-coloring mechanism is not yet implemented. This scaffold's baseline placeholder reuses the existing spatial-linkage composite (Uberon-only join, placeholder readout) purely so the study resolves and renders; wiring real dataset values onto `readout` is future work.

biological_summary:
spatial-linkage proved the join topology is correct and deterministic (10
links across 5 models, exactly 2 nodes per model — one per sex GLB) but
every link's `readout` field is a literal placeholder string
("pending time-series"): no simulation result is actually attached to a
scene node yet. The committed full-corpus COPASI/Tellurium comparison
dataset (used by glucose-biomodel-do and glucose-regulation for
cross-engine agreement) already contains per-species time-course data for
several of the same linked models (e.g. BIOMD0000000633's hepatic glucose
species). This study is the natural next step: pull a steady-state value
per linked species out of that existing dataset and attach it as the
link's real readout, so a downstream 3D viewer can finally color AS nodes
by biological result, not just by which organ has a model at all.
limitations: TBD — planned study, not yet implemented.

remaining_uncertainties: Can we spatially link model RESULTS (steady-state values), not just organ presence, to a specific AS node?
